h1: Niagara Falls travel, stays & events guide
heroText: Niagara Falls is a Canada base best planned around named sights rather than a generic stopover. Start with Horseshoe Falls, add Journey Behind the Falls, and use Clifton Hill to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Niagara Falls International Airport handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Niagara Falls International Airport and central Niagara Falls before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Start with City centre for the easiest first Niagara Falls stay, then compare Old Town and Waterfront when price, nightlife, quieter evenings or transfer timing matter more than being beside every major sight.
hotelIntro: Niagara Falls hotel choice is mostly about repeat journeys: use City centre for sightseeing, Old Town for a different local base, and Waterfront or Airport area when views, parking, airport timing or longer stays matter.
rentalCars: Do not rent a car for central Niagara Falls unless parking and traffic are part of the plan; use one mainly for regional day trips.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose City centre for a first stay because it keeps main sights, restaurants and practical local movement close.

travelTips.title: Airport timing
travelTips.text: Leave extra time for Niagara Falls International Airport, especially for early flights, late arrivals, traffic or unfamiliar transfer routes.

travelTips.title: Local movement
travelTips.text: Plan each day in clusters around Horseshoe Falls and Journey Behind the Falls so transfers do not consume the best sightseeing hours.

travelTips.title: Day trips
travelTips.text: Keep one flexible slot for nearby routes from Niagara Falls, checking weather, transport and opening hours before committing.

history.text: The property was sold off and split in 1898 and went through several ownership changes until Walter Schoellkopf (1882–1955) bought the property in 1916.
Included in the purchase were unique furnishings, including dinner chairs used during a visit to the area in 1919 by Edward, Prince of Wales (the future King Edward VIII).
The Schoellkopf family was from across the Niagara River in Niagara Falls, New York, and they were pioneers of hydraulic power development in the region. Sir Harry Oakes In 1924, Harry Oakes and his.

After Oakes' death in the Bahamas in 1943, Lady Oakes deeded the mansion to the Government of Canada to be used as a convalescent hospital for the Royal Canadian Air Force.
In 1952, when the government no longer needed the home, it was deeded back to the Oakes family.
